🚨TODAY is the last day to enroll in the health insurance marketplace for coverage beginning on February 1.

To sign up, make changes to your existing plan, or learn more about your options, you can visit https://t.co/0xBj9mT1WP or call +1 (800) 318-2596.
March is National Nutrition Month. As the only Virginian on the House Ag Committee, I’m committed to safeguarding programs like SNAP that keep Virginia’s families fed. https://t.co/4hLVfgVg1n

Dairy farmers in Virginia have THREE DAYS to sign up for Dairy Margin Coverage by the March 31st deadline at their local FSA office. 🐄🥛

If you have questions or need assistance, you can contact my office at (703) 987-2180.
https://t.co/c1qBw16kjv https://t.co/uxchAxfL1A

The Patrick Leahy Farm to School Program supports local farmers, provides important nutrition education, and gets healthy food to Virginia students.

I joined 38 of my colleagues in demanding answers as to why @USDA cut this vital program. https://t.co/ijopC4is5m

Today, I’m wearing turquoise to raise awareness of those living with lung cancer — which disproportionately impacts firefighters and veterans.

In Congress, I am committed to fighting for policy that supports prevention, detection, and treatment of this terrible disease.🩵 https://t.co/KfFdpVtvEa

This morning, my team enjoyed checking out the community health and wellness expo at Gar-Field High School in Woodbridge.
 
At this event, @NC100BWinc provided free health screenings and health education resources to our neighbors in PWC. Thank you for all you do! https://t.co/I6UVRDxMgy

🚜VA-07: Key crop insurance deadlines are coming up, with major sales closing dates on May 1, July 15, and July 31.

Coverage options help you manage risk and protect operations — so don’t wait. Visit https://t.co/vJYxgltYFf or contact your crop insurance agent to learn more.

This week, I toured @UVA Health's Culpeper Medical Center and met with hospital leadership.

I enjoyed learning more about their thriving nurse workforce pipeline and state-of-the-art cancer treatment center. We even heard the bells that chime throughout the hospital when a baby is born!

Forcing a 4-year-old U.S. citizen with Stage 4 cancer to be deported with his mother and sister tears him from his doctors, his treatment, and his rights.

This isn’t border security — it’s cruelty.

American children shouldn’t be casualties of a secure border.

It was a gorgeous day to participate in Supervisor Andrea Bailey’s annual 5K raising awareness for mental health resources. 

I enjoyed running alongside Marines from Marine Corps Base Quantico and joining so many folks in getting their exercise! https://t.co/JqbaZAMUgm

I was deeply saddened to hear of President Biden's cancer diagnosis.

Cancer is a horrible disease that has touched every life in one way or another. Cindy and I join the American people in wishing him strength during this difficult time.

Last night, a callous, dangerous, and partisan bill passed with solely Republican support — and they did it while Americans were asleep, hoping no one would notice. 

I am outraged and disgusted. I cannot fathom how extreme Republicans can sleep soundly after rubber stamping the largest cuts to basic needs programs for healthcare and hunger in my lifetime. (1/6)

June is Alzheimer’s & Brain Awareness Month. In Virginia, more than 150,000 people live with Alzheimer's. 

This month, may we honor those navigating this disease and recommit to our fight for better research, treatment, and care. #ENDALZ

The Supreme Court just gave states the green light to block Medicaid patients from accessing care at Planned Parenthood.

This decision will mean fewer available reproductive health services, delayed cancer diagnoses, and more maternal deaths.

This will cost lives.

Congratulations to Sharon Gregory for being named Virginia’s Adapted P.E. Teacher of the Year!

I appreciate your dedication to helping children with special needs participate in organized sports and exercise.

Thank you for your years of service.
https://t.co/ZKNLChav1R

I wouldn’t be able to sleep at night if I voted to rip health care away from 17 million Americans.

Apparently, some of my colleagues can.

I voted NO on Trump’s budget the first time it came to the House — and I’ll do it again.

The economy is struggling and costs are out of control. Meanwhile, extreme Washington Republicans just voted to make sure 3-year-old Luka, my constituent who relies on Medicaid, has a much harder life – it’s just cruel. I don’t know how my colleagues sleep soundly after voting for a bill that will cost people their lives. 1/4

Republicans voted to rip health care away from 300,000 Virginians, cut vital food assistance like SNAP, and shutter rural hospitals.

Why did they vote for this chaos and cruelty? To give tax breaks to their ultra wealthy friends, of course.
https://t.co/Cy7LoAbo08

This week, I spoke with more than 7,500 Virginians on my latest telephone town hall.

Folks are angry — and rightfully so — about Trump’s budget that will slash Medicaid and SNAP.

I’ll keep standing up for families and the programs that keep them afloat.

Trump's Big, Ugly Bill is cutting lifesaving programs — like SNAP and Medicaid — for millions of Americans.

I am appalled that hardworking Americans are being treated as collateral damage as Trump cuts taxes for billionaires.

President Johnson signed Medicare and Medicaid into law 60 years ago, expanding affordable health care to millions.

But right now, these programs are under threat due to the GOP budget that will close rural hospitals and slash the health care of more than 320,000 Virginians.

In Congress, I'm committed to working hard to deliver the quality, affordable health care that every Virginian and American across our country deserves.

FACT: Cruel GOP cuts to Medicaid will cost 300,000 Virginians their health care — including tens of thousands of residents of the Seventh District.

I didn’t come to Congress to sit idly by while the communities I serve lose access to care. I’ll keep standing up for families because they deserve peace of mind.

Ripping health care away from 1/3 of the nearly 415,000 Virginians covered through the ACA isn’t the answer.
 
By refusing to extend tax credits, extreme Washington Republicans would force many to go without essential care.
 
I won’t stand idly by while Virginians lose coverage.

I will support a budget bill that protects Virginians' healthcare, invests in public schools, and lowers costs for hardworking families.
 
That is what the American people overwhelmingly want.

I hope I get a chance to vote for that — but it certainly wasn’t on the floor today. https://t.co/cJwdfblfDv

The Trump administration has canceled USDA’s annual food insecurity survey — the very tool that measures hunger in America.

This is a blatant attempt to hide rising food insecurity and the impact of cuts to federal nutrition programs.
